deep_dive.title: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
deep_dive.abstract: Single-cell perturbation screens are used to train and evaluate models that predict perturbation effects, and model scores are judged against how reproducible the measured effects are. Reproducibility is usually judged by splitting each perturbation's cells into two random halves. This assumes that the halves are independent replicates. In pooled screens such as Perturb-seq, however, the cells carrying a guide RNA descend from a limited number of transduced cells, so two random halves contain the same clones: pseudoreplication whose unit is not marked in the data. Using perturbations that should have no effect as controls, we compared random halves with independent replicates from separate transductions, and tested directly with halves that differ only in their clones. In a genome-scale screen of primary T cells, null perturbations agreed between random halves almost always and between independent replicates only half the time, the rate expected from noise alone; measuring more cells did not remove this agreement. Splitting the cells into halves that share no clone, by the T-cell receptor constant region or by a clone barcode, largely removed the excess agreement. Its size equals the share of expression differences set by clones divided by the effective number of clones per perturbation; across 16 screens it was largest in T cells transferred into mice and in a genome-scale primary T-cell screen, one to two orders of magnitude smaller in cell lines, and smallest in non-dividing neurons. Shared clones inflate benchmark ceilings and reliability labels, and when a model's input and its scoring answer come from one transduction, published models that predict perturbation effects in a new cell state appear better than a baseline that ignores the perturbation; against cells from another transduction, most fall below it. Reproducibility should be judged across separate transductions.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Splitting a perturbation's cells into random halves is standard for judging reproducibility of single-cell perturbation screens, but shared clones make the halves pseudoreplicates, inflating reproducibility and biasing model evaluation.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 在Perturb-seq等单细胞扰动筛选中，评估扰动效应预测模型常以同一扰动的细胞随机对半分来估计可重复性，但同一克隆来源使两半并非独立重复，构成伪重复。作者以预期无效应的对照扰动为基准，比较随机对半与来自不同转导的独立重复，并直接检验克隆结构不同的两半。结果表明随机对半会高估可重复性，使模型评分偏乐观。该工作为单细胞扰动响应预测模型的训练与评测提供了更可靠的统计标准。
